title: Stellara Labs - Dedicated Capacity Discovery
summary: Stellara is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for low-latency inference of multi-model recommendation and retrieval systems. Main concerns: strict data isolation, predictable throughput for peak shopping events, burst to hosted capacity, and SLOs. Next steps: share pricing/commit tiers, security pack (SOC2 docs), and set up a short benchmark run with synthetic traffic and a 2-week pilot proposal.
action_items: Maya Chen - Send Dedicated pricing tiers and example reserved capacity contracts by 2025-10-07
Ethan Park - Share benchmarking template and ask-for-data sheet (model sizes, QPS, tail latency targets) by 2025-10-06
Amir Desai - Provide 7-day peak QPS and current model lineup by 2025-10-08
next_steps: Redwood to send security pack (SOC2, ISO) and KMS integration notes
Schedule 30-min benchmark kickoff with SE + infra on next Thu
Propose 2-week pilot with 2x reserved gpus + burst to hosted during initial run
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-02
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Amir (Stellara CTO), Ruth (ML Eng), Lena (Infra)

00:00 Maya: Okay hi everyone, thanks for joining. we're looking to learn more about Stellara's usage and figure out whether Dedicated or Private makes sense. quick intro round?
00:10 Amir: Hey I'm Amir, CTO. we run recommendation + retrieval for e-comm, traffic spikes during promos are our biggest pain. tail latency needs to be under 120ms p95 for critical requests.
00:24 Ruth: Ruth here, i own the models - we have two ensembles, a 7B reranker and a 13B generator for product descriptions. currently hosted on k8s with GPU nodes.
00:38 Lena: Lena, infra - security and VPC requirements. we need network isolation and audit logs, also KMS for keys.
00:47 Maya: great thanks. Ethan from Redwood will go into the nitty gritty on capacity and burst.
00:54 Ethan: hi all. quick question to start: what's your current steady QPS and peak during events?
01:03 Amir: Steady is ~250 qps across endpoints, peaks go up to 1.2k during flash sales for 20-30 minutes, and we sometimes see sustained 500 qps for an hour or two.
01:18 Ethan: ok that's helpful. and what's your latency target for the critical path? you mentioned 120ms p95, is that end-to-end including network?
01:28 Amir: yes, end-to-end is what product measures. we can relax non-critical generation to 300ms.
01:36 Ethan: got it. rough question on model sizes and batching: your 13B generator - is that fp16, any quantization today?
01:43 Ruth: currently fp16, no quant. latency is borderline, we tried 8-bit but saw accuracy drop.
01:51 Ethan: understood. Dedicated reserved GPUs can help with predictability. typically for ensembles like yours we recommend a mix: reserved pool for steady throughput and autoscaled burst capacity to handle spikes.
02:05 Amir: can you burst to hosted? we can't expose customer data, so burst to shared hosted could be a problem.
02:12 Ethan: yes thats a common question. Redwood supports burst to hosted if customers allow sending non-sensitive inference requests; for sensitive payloads we can burst to a private capacity or we can provide a hybrid where ephemeral seats are still within your VPC in Private mode - there's a couple of options.
02:27 Lena: let me pause there - data residency and isolation is non-negotiable for parts of our pipeline. we need audit logs, SSO, and KMS.
02:36 Maya: totally. for Dedicated we provide network isolation at the tenant level (VPC peering / PrivateLink), KMS integrations, and audit logs. we also have a Private deployment option if you need full control.
02:48 Ruth: for the reranker, we do a lot of cold-starts - will KV cache be shared? we've seen cache thrash on previous infra.
02:56 Ethan: KV cache is per-instance in our runtime, but with Dedicated you can get reserved nodes pinned to your pool so cold-starts are reduced. We can also configure prefix caching and warm up policies. sometimes transcription says K V cache, but it's the same.
03:12 Amir: whats the typical reserved GPU commit you see for customers with similar profiles?
03:19 Ethan: for ~250 steady qps with 1.2k peaks, we usually see customers start with an N+1 reserved pool. e.g., 8x A100-equivalent slots reserved with autoscale rules that add 4-8 more on burst, depending on burst duration. pricing can be a deciding factor, so we'll model cost per qps.
03:38 Maya: and we offer burst-to-hosted as a policy toggle - you can set sensitive routes to never burst, others may. So it's flexible.
03:48 Lena: what's the failover behavior if reserved pool is saturated? do you degrade gracefully?
03:55 Ethan: yes, we have smart routing and fallbacks: route to compatible model variants (e.g., quantized smaller model), or queue with a small backpressure window. can also route to hosted if allowed. we'll show options in the runbook.
04:12 Amir: how does scaling latency behave during autoscale? we worry about sudden spike and cold-start overhead.
04:20 Ethan: autoscale for Dedicated is GPU-level; we have warm spare instances in the pool and continuous batching to reduce cold start. typical scale takes 30-90s depending on model size; for hard SLOs we do pre-warm when a scheduled promo is known.
04:35 Ruth: can you do scheduled scaling? we have predictable promo windows for Black Friday style events.
04:40 Ethan: yes scheduled policies are available, including pre-warm kernel selection and pre-provisioned capacity. we also support autoscale based on queue depth and p95 latency signals.
04:53 Maya: security: we'll send SOC2 and ISO docs plus our KMS integration guide. Lena, is there anything else you need?
05:00 Lena: SSH access? not necessary, but we need audit log retention policy and map to Splunk. also want RBAC and SAML SSO.
05:10 Maya: we support RBAC, SAML/SSO, and audit logs shipped via syslog/forwarder to SIEMs. retention tiers are configurable with add-on.
05:20 Amir: on pricing: how do committed reserved GPU contracts look? term lengths and overage rules?
05:27 Maya: we have monthly and annual reserved commitments. typical starter pilots are 3 months with an option to convert to annual for discount. overage can be billed at a higher rate or you can allow burst credits to cover short spikes.
05:41 Ruth: will we be able to pin model versions for canary and rollouts? we need consistent inference across versions.
05:48 Ethan: yes version pinning, canary rollouts, and automatic rollback based on eval metrics are in the console. also token-level cost and latency breakdowns in our dashboard.
05:58 Amir: about benchmarks: can you run a synthetic benchmark with our models or do you need us to provide artifacts?
06:06 Ethan: we prefer you give model artifacts and a representative workload; we can run a hosted benchmark or run within a dedicated pilot. for secure artifacts we can sign an NDA and run inside a private test environment.
06:18 Maya: next steps: we'll send pricing, security pack, and a short data ask. propose benchmark kickoff next Thu.
06:25 Amir: sounds good. couple of other Qs: what about quantization recommendations? we tried int8 but saw quality drop.
06:33 Ethan: our Optimize tooling suggests per-model quantization profiles based on evals. sometimes int8 works for rerankers, but generators often need careful tuning. we can run evals on your prompt sets to measure regressed outputs.
06:47 Ruth: on the topic of model split - i.e., running encoder/decoder across different nodes - is that supported? we've split components before to save memory.
06:56 Ethan: the runtime supports sharded/partitioned execution and can place different components on different GPUs. it's part of how we optimize kernel selection and memory.
07:10 Amir: any gotchas with our current k8s setup migrating to Dedicated?
07:15 Maya: we'll provide a migration plan. customers often containerize model servers or use our model registry; we assist with mapping model artifacts, quantization picks, and routing policies.
07:27 Lena: how are logs and metrics exported? we need Prometheus metrics and traces.
07:32 Ethan: we export Prometheus, have tracing hooks, and raw logs can be forwarded. console gives per-route latency and token cost.
07:41 Amir: ok i want an example cost model for 8 reserved GPUs vs 12 reserved with burst. can you send that?
07:48 Maya: yes will do.
07:51 Ruth: do you support hardware variation - e.g., we prefer H100 for generator latency but A100 was cheaper previously.
07:58 Ethan: we support multiple instance types; kernel selection varies. we recommend H100 for large generator low-latency, but we can quantify cost/performance tradeoffs in the model report.
08:09 Amir: great. any security questionnaires to fill? we have a procurement checklist.
08:14 Maya: we will send template responses; if needed we'll engage security team for an RFP call.
08:20 (crosstalk)
08:25 Maya: to recap: Redwood will send pricing and security pack, SE to share benchmark template, Stellara to share baseline traffic and model artifacts, and then we'll schedule a benchmark kickoff.
08:40 Amir: sounds good, thank you.
08:44 Maya: thanks everyone.

Note: transcription contains minor errors and occasional mis-attributed speakers, some technical terms (KV cache, kernel selection) are sometimes split or hyphenated oddly.
